title: Claude for Legal adds checklists that link every line to a source
friendlyTitle: Claude for Legal now starts the check, then points at the source
summary: Anthropic added a gallery of ready-made artifacts for Claude for Legal. The six it highlights are a cite check, a jurisdiction survey, a matter board, a playbook deviation board, a regulatory timeline, and a table pulled from a stack of contracts. Each one opens with an example. A lawyer adds documents or connectors, Claude does a first pass, and every answer links back to the source language. Anthropic says it has added more than 60 legal connectors since the May launch, including Bloomberg Law.
friendlySummary: Anthropic added ready-made tools for Claude for Legal. The six it highlights check whether a quote matches its source, compare a legal topic across places, turn a pile of matters into one board, flag contract clauses that differ from your standard terms, map upcoming rules on a timeline, and build a table from a stack of contracts. Each tool opens with an example. A lawyer adds the documents. Claude does a first pass. Every answer links back to the original words. Anthropic says it has added more than 60 legal connections since May, including Bloomberg Law.
whyItMatters: The design is a first draft with a citation, not a finished opinion. A cite check flags quotes that do not match, wrong page numbers, and sources that do not support the claim. A person still has to read the flag. Sharing settings are meant to keep client walls in place, which is Anthropic's claim, not an audit. If your legal work is still a pile of uploads, the connector list is the part worth checking before the templates.
